questions.question:
Identify the degree of comparison of the underlined adjective in the statutory clause:
"The Chief Justice shall assign the matter to the most experienced bench available in the roster."

options.text: Comparative Degree
Positive Degree
Superlative Degree
Absolute Positive Degree

questions.explanation: Adjective 'experienced' multi-syllabic participial adjective hai jiske sath periphrastic marker 'most' aur definite article 'the' laga hua hai ('the most experienced'). Ye High Court roster ke sabhi available benches mein se apex bench ko designate kar raha hai. Isliye ye conclusively Superlative Degree hai. Comparative 'more experienced' hota hai aur positive 'experienced' hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: The + most + multi-syllable adjective constitutes the Superlative Degree.
questions.hint: 'The most experienced' roster ke sabhi benches mein apex level ko denote karta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.subtopic: CVC Consonant Doubling in Legal Context
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelled comparative form of 'fit':
"After physical re-examination, the applicant was declared ___ for the post than previously assessed."

options.text: fiter
fitter
more fit
fittest

questions.explanation: Word 'fit' monosyllabic adjective hai jo consonant 't' par end hota hai aur usse theek pehle single short vowel 'i' hai (CVC pattern). Rule ke anusaar, '-er' jodne se pehle final consonant double hota hai: f-i-t + t + e-r = 'fitter'. Option (A) single 't' spelling error hai. Option (C) unnecessary periphrasis hai. Option (D) superlative form hai jabki sentence mein do assessments compare ho rahe hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: CVC pattern adjectives double their final consonant before '-er'.
questions.hint: Single vowel + single consonant hone par comparative form mein consonant double ho jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Select the appropriate form to complete the official performance review:
"The typing accuracy of Candidate A is ___ than that of Candidate B."

options.text: gooder
more good
better
best

questions.explanation: Adjective 'good' irregular suppletion follow karta hai: good ➔ better ➔ best. Conjunction 'than' do candidates ('Candidate A' vs 'Candidate B') ke beech comparative degree demand karta hai, isliye correct form 'better' hai. English mein '*gooder' ya '*more good' completely incorrect hain. Option (D) 'best' superlative hai jo do entities ke comparison mein nahi lag sakta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Irregular grading of good / well ➔ better ➔ best.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Choose the correct comparative adjective for the blank:
"The state government has ___ financial liability under the modified scheme than under the original contract."

options.text: littler
more little
less
least

questions.explanation: Noun 'liability' (in terms of financial amount) uncountable noun hai jiska positive quantifier 'little' hota hai. 'Little' ka comparative degree 'less' (ya 'lesser') hota hai aur superlative 'least' hota hai. English mein '*littler' ya '*more little' non-standard hain. Conjunction 'than' do schemes ke beech comparison indicate kar raha hai, isliye comparative 'less' aayega. Option (D) superlative hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Little (amount) ➔ less / lesser (comparative) ➔ least (superlative).
questions.hint: 'Little' ka comparative amount form 'less' hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the positive sentence into an equivalent comparative sentence:
"The junior clerk is as competent as the record keeper."

options.text: The record keeper is more competent than the junior clerk.
The record keeper is not more competent than the junior clerk.
The junior clerk is more competent than the record keeper.
The record keeper is the most competent officer.

questions.explanation: Original sentence equality show kar raha hai ('as competent as'), yaani dono barabar competent hain. Comparative transformation mein ye meaning preserve hona chahiye ki record keeper junior clerk se zyada competent nahi hai ('is not more competent than'). Option (A) aur (C) ek ko doosre se superior declare kar dete hain jisse original parity toot jati hai. Option (D) superlative statement hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Equality 'as...as' transforms to negative comparative 'not more...than'.
questions.hint: Dono barabar hain. Isliye comparative mein negative aayega: 'is NOT more competent than'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the comparative sentence into a positive sentence preserving its exact propositional meaning:
"The public prosecutor was more persuasive than the defense counsel."

options.text: The defense counsel was not as persuasive as the public prosecutor.
The public prosecutor was not as persuasive as the defense counsel.
The defense counsel was as persuasive as the public prosecutor.
No other advocate was as persuasive as the public prosecutor.

questions.explanation: Original sentence kehta hai public prosecutor defense counsel se zyada persuasive tha (prosecutor > defense). Positive transformation mein: (1) Inferior entity 'The defense counsel' subject banega; (2) Sentence negative banega ('was not'); (3) Adjective base positive form mein 'as persuasive as' ke beech aayega: 'The defense counsel was not as persuasive as the public prosecutor.' Option (B) meaning ulta kar deta hai. Option (C) parity assert karta hai. Option (D) scope ko universal bana deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: S1 + Comp + than + S2 ➔ S2 + not as/so + Positive + as + S1.
questions.hint: Defense counsel kam persuasive tha, isliye sentence banega: 'The defense counsel was not as persuasive as...'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Choose the correct comparative transformation of:
"Iron is the most useful of all metals."

options.text: Iron is more useful than any metal.
Iron is more useful than any other metal.
Iron is more useful than any other metals.
Iron is more useful than most other metals.

questions.explanation: 'The most useful of all metals' unique apex superlative hai. Comparative transformation mein iron ko baaki metals se alag karne ke liye 'any other' lagana mandatory hai, aur 'any other' ke baad strictly singular countable noun 'metal' aayega: 'Iron is more useful than any other metal.' Option (A) mein 'other' missing hai jo self-exclusion violation hai. Option (C) plural 'metals' use karta hai jo 'any other' ke sath galat hai. Option (D) 'most other' subset group ('one of the') ke liye use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05 & RC-06: The + Superlative ➔ Comparative + than ANY OTHER + Singular Noun.
questions.hint: 'More useful than' ke sath 'any other' aur singular noun 'metal' aana chahiye.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the comparative sentence into a positive sentence:
"Shakespeare is greater than any other English dramatist."

options.text: No other English dramatist is as great as Shakespeare.
No other English dramatists are as great as Shakespeare.
Very few English dramatists are as great as Shakespeare.
Shakespeare is as great as any English dramatist.

questions.explanation: Comparative construction 'greater than any other English dramatist' unique apex denote karti hai. Iska positive transformation 'NO OTHER + Singular Noun + is + as...as' se start hota hai: 'No other English dramatist is as great as Shakespeare.' Option (B) plural noun 'dramatists' aur plural verb 'are' use karta hai jo 'No other' ke rule ke against hai. Option (C) 'Very few' subset ranking ke liye hota hai. Option (D) affirmative general parity state karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Comparative + than any other + Singular Noun ➔ NO OTHER + Singular Noun + is + as...as.
questions.hint: Sentence 'No other English dramatist' (singular noun + singular verb 'is') se shuru hona chahiye.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the positive sentence into a superlative sentence:
"No other river in the world is as long as the Nile."

options.text: The Nile is longest river in the world.
The Nile is the longest river in the world.
The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world.
The Nile is longer than all rivers in the world.

questions.explanation: 'No other river... is as long as the Nile' state karta hai ki duniya ki koi doosri river Nile jitni lambi nahi hai (Nile is number-1). Superlative transformation mein Nile subject banega, definite article 'the' aayega, aur 'the longest river in the world' banega: 'The Nile is the longest river in the world.' Option (A) mein mandatory article 'the' missing hai. Option (C) 'one of the' lagakar ise top bracket bana deta hai. Option (D) comparative form hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: NO OTHER + Singular Noun ➔ Subject + is + THE + Superlative + Singular Noun.
questions.hint: Superlative degree mein article 'the' lagakar 'the longest river' choose karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.subtopic: Subset Group: 'One of the' to Comparative
questions.question:
Transform the superlative sentence into a comparative sentence:
"Tagore was one of the greatest poets of India."

options.text: Tagore was greater than any other poet of India.
Tagore was greater than most other poets of India.
Tagore was greater than most other poet of India.
No other poet of India was greater than Tagore.

questions.explanation: Original sentence 'one of the greatest poets' indicate karta hai ki Tagore top elite poets ke group mein shamil the (akela unique supreme nahi the). Iska comparative transformation strictly 'than MOST OTHER + PLURAL NOUN' se hota hai: 'Tagore was greater than most other poets of India.' Option (A) 'any other' lagakar Tagore ko akela number-1 bana deta hai (meaning distortion). Option (C) singular 'poet' use karta hai jo 'most other' ke sath galat hai. Option (D) negative comparison banata hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: One of the + Superlative + Plural Noun ➔ Comparative + than MOST OTHER + Plural Noun.
questions.hint: 'One of the' ke comparative transformation mein 'any other' nahi, 'than most other poets' (plural) lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.subtopic: Subset Group: 'One of the' to Positive
questions.question:
Choose the correct positive transformation of:
"Udaipur is one of the most beautiful cities in India."

options.text: No other city in India is as beautiful as Udaipur.
Very few cities in India are as beautiful as Udaipur.
Very few city in India is as beautiful as Udaipur.
Udaipur is as beautiful as all cities in India.

questions.explanation: 'One of the most beautiful cities' subset group ko represent kar raha hai. Iska positive transformation hamesha 'VERY FEW + Plural Noun + Plural Verb' se hota hai: 'Very few cities in India are as beautiful as Udaipur.' Option (A) 'No other' unique number-1 city bana deta hai (scope change). Option (C) singular noun 'city' aur singular verb 'is' use karta hai jo 'Very few' ke sath grammatically incorrect hai. Option (D) general parity assert karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: One of the ➔ VERY FEW + Plural Noun + Plural Verb + as...as.
questions.hint: 'One of the' ka positive transformation 'Very few cities... are' se start hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Spot the error in the underlined parts of the sentence:
"The senior judge (A) / is more respected (B) / than any member (C) / of the district bar association. (D)"

options.text: Part (A)
Part (B)
Part (C)
Part (D)

questions.explanation: Part (C) mein error hai. Yahan judge (jo bar association ke members ke category mein evaluate ho raha hai) ko uske group se exclude karne ke liye word 'other' missing hai. Sentence hona chahiye 'than any other member' (NOT: 'than any member'). 'Other' ke bina judge khud se bhi compare hone lagta hai jo logical self-inclusion error hai. Parts (A), (B), aur (D) grammatically correct hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: The 'Any Other' Self-Exclusion Law — 'other' is mandatory when comparing within the same class.
questions.hint: Part (C) mein 'than any member' likha hai jisme word 'other' missing hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the grammatically correct phrase:
"Of the two candidates interviewed for the system assistant post, Ravi is ___."

options.text: the most competent
the more competent
more competent
most competent

questions.explanation: Sentence clearly specify kar raha hai 'Of the two candidates' (strictly DO candidates). Rule: Jab total entities strictly 2 hon, toh Superlative Degree ('the most competent') lagana strict error hai. Do entities ke beech selection mein comparative degree use hoti hai aur comparative se pehle definite article 'THE' lagta hai: 'Ravi is THE MORE COMPETENT'. Option (A) aur (D) superlative use kar rahe hain jo do entities ke case mein invalid hain. Option (C) mein required article 'the' missing hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: When comparing exactly two entities, use 'THE + Comparative' ('the more competent of the two').
questions.hint: Do candidates ke beech 'the most' nahi balki 'the more' aayega.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly adheres to the rules of Latin comparatives?

options.text: The junior court assistant is junior than the bench clerk.
The junior court assistant is more junior than the bench clerk.
The junior court assistant is junior to the bench clerk.
The junior court assistant is more junior to the bench clerk.

questions.explanation: Latin comparatives (junior, senior, superior, inferior, prior) conjunction 'than' nahi lete; strictly preposition 'TO' demand karte hain. Sath hi, ye words already comparative force express karte hain, isliye inke pehle 'more' lagana redundant double comparative error hai. Isliye strictly Option (C) 'junior to' grammatically flawless hai. Option (A) mein 'than' hai, Option (B) mein 'more' aur 'than' dono hain, aur Option (D) mein 'more' redundant hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Latin Comparatives take 'TO' (never 'than', never 'more').
questions.hint: 'Junior' ke baad 'to' lagta hai aur 'more' bilkul nahi lagta.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence comparing two qualities of the SAME individual:
"The senior advocate was ___ than ___ in conducting the cross-examination."

options.text: bolder than discreet
more bold than discreet
boldest than discreet
more bolder than discreet

questions.explanation: Rule: Jab do alag individuals ka comparison na ho raha ho balki EK HI INDIVIDUAL KI DO QUALITIES (boldness vs discretion) ka comparison ho raha ho, toh single-syllable adjective hone ke bawjood '-er' suffix use nahi ho sakta; strictly 'MORE + base adjective' use hota hai: 'The senior advocate was more bold than discreet.' Option (A) '-er' suffix use karta hai jo do alag logon ke liye hota hai. Option (C) superlative hai. Option (D) double comparative error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Single Entity Two Qualities ➔ Strictly 'MORE [Adj 1] than [Adj 2]'.
questions.hint: Ek hi advocate ki do qualities compare ho rahi hain, isliye '-er' ki jagah 'more bold' aayega.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09
